findings.issue: Server handlers rely on ambient auto-imported h3 helpers (defineEventHandler, getRouterParam) rather than explicit imports from the new 'nuxt/server' surface introduced in Nuxt 4.6 (same pattern in move/type/ability/[name].get.ts and pokedex.get.ts).
findings.suggestion: Explicitly `import { defineEventHandler, getRouterParam } from 'nuxt/server'` so the handlers run unchanged on Nuxt 5 (Nitro v3 / h3 v2). Supported but optional on Nuxt 4 — no urgency.

findings.issue: compatibilityDate '2025-07-15' is over a year old relative to the pinned Nuxt 4.6.3 (2026-10-27), so the app opts out of newer default behavior Nuxt considers stable.
findings.suggestion: Bump compatibilityDate to the current date (or the 4.6 release date) to pick up the current stable defaults; verify tests still pass.

findings.issue: `definePageMeta({})` is an empty no-op call left in the page.
findings.suggestion: Delete the line; definePageMeta should only be used when it carries keys.

summary: This is a maximally conservative Nuxt app: zero experimental flags, zero preview/RC APIs, and a dependency set of exactly one package (nuxt, pinned to the current stable 4.6.3, which conveniently patches a fresh security advisory). Everything it does is built on APIs stable since Nuxt 3, all data access is wrapped behind its own /api/* server routes, so even the one genuinely new surface in Nuxt 4.6 (nuxt/server imports) is untouched. The only forward-compat nudge worth a review comment is adopting explicit nuxt/server imports before Nuxt 5.
